chunks.title: Lior Veylan
chunks.text: Raised as a moisture farmer on the desert planet Sovar, Lior joins the Freeworld Concord and becomes a pivotal figure in its struggle against the Vastran Dominion. He trains as a Vaelari Knight under the Vaelari Masters Orven Tal and Ulmor, and eventually confronts his father, the Nerathi Lord Vhar Kordane. Years later, Lior trains his nephew Renik Darell and mentors the scavenger Zerra. Lior is the twin brother of Nira Solenne.

chunks.title: Lior Veylan
chunks.text: Lior changes his mind when he finds that Dominion armored legionaries have killed his aunt and uncle. He and Orven travel to Namar Port, where they meet the smugglers Taren Darell and Ruvakka. They hire the duo to take them to Elaris on the Vesper Kite, only to discover that it has been destroyed by the Abyss Sphere, the Dominion's battle station. The Kite is brought to the Abyss Sphere via capture beam, and Lior and Taren disguise themselves as armored legionaries to infiltrate the station. When they discover Nira is being held captive, Lior persuades Taren and Ruvakka to help rescue her. Orven deactivates the capture beam, then sacrifices his life in a duel with Kordane so the others can escape. Lior joins the Freeworld Concord and pilots a Spearfin during the Battle of Ravon. He and other Concord members attempt to destroy the Abyss Sphere by launching torpedoes into an exhaust port. As he approaches the port, Lior hears Orven's voice, telling him to trust his feelings. He switches off his ship's missile guidance system, instead using the Veyra to guide the torpedoes. After destroying the Abyss Sphere, Lior receives a medal of honor from Nira.

chunks.title: Vhar Kordane
chunks.text: Aren Veylan's transformation into Vhar Kordane begins when he is lured to the dark side of the Veyra by Chancellor Sereth, who later becomes the Galactic Sovereign. After a lumenblade battle with his former mentor Orven Tal, Kordane is severely injured and is transformed into a cyborg. He serves Sereth for over two decades, hunting down the remaining Vaelari and attempting to crush the Freeworld Concord. When Sereth tries to kill Kordane's son, Lior Veylan, Kordane turns against Sereth and kills him. Kordane is the husband of Selya Mereth, the father of Lior and his twin sister Nira Solenne, and the maternal grandfather of Renik Darell (later known as Vhar Soreth).

chunks.title: Vhar Kordane
chunks.text: Vhar Kordane is a cyborg commander serving the Vastran Dominion. He and Governor Varrik have been tasked with recovering architectural plans for the Abyss Sphere battle station, which were stolen by the Freeworld Concord. Kordane captures and interrogates the Concord leader Princess Nira, who has sent the plans to Kordane's former master Orven Tal. During Nira's rescue by Orven's allies Lior Veylan and Taren Darell, Kordane strikes down his former mentor in a lumenblade duel. After placing a tracking device aboard Taren's ship, Kordane locates the Concord base on Ravon 4. When the Concord members attack the Abyss Sphere, Kordane pursues Lior in his VEX fighter. Before he can shoot Lior down, however, Taren intervenes and sends Kordane's ship spiraling off course, which allows Lior to destroy the Abyss Sphere.

chunks.title: Princess Nira
chunks.text:
Princess Nira of Elaris is a member of the Dominion Assembly and a leader in the Freeworld Concord. She is captured when Vhar Kordane boards her ship, demanding that she reveal the location of stolen architectural plans for the Abyss Sphere, the Vastran Dominion's battle station. Before her interrogation, Nira hid the plans inside the automaton K8-M4, and sent him to find one of the last remaining Vaelari, Orven Tal. Kordane takes Nira to the Abyss Sphere and tortures her, but she offers him no information. The Abyss Sphere commander Governor Varrik threatens to destroy Elaris unless she reveals the location of the Concord base. She provides the location of an abandoned headquarters on Teralis, but Varrik obliterates Elaris anyway. Nira is rescued by Lior Veylan, Taren Darell and Ruvakka. They escape aboard Taren's ship, the Vesper Kite. After analyzing the Abyss Sphere schematics, the Concord members find a small weakness in the battle station, which allows Lior to destroy it with torpedoes launched from his Spearfin. After the victory, Nira honors Lior, Taren and Ruvakka for their heroism.

Nira's father is Aren Veylan, a Vaelari who falls to the dark side of the Veyra and becomes Vhar Kordane. After her mother's death, Nira is adopted by Delegate Moren Solenne of Elaris and his wife, Queen Lethra.

chunks.title: Taren Darell
chunks.text: Taren Darell and his Ruunak co-pilot Ruvakka accept a charter to transport Lior Veylan and Orven Tal from Sovar to Elaris on their ship, the Vesper Kite. Before they depart, Darell is cornered by the bounty hunter Heskor, who threatens him. Darell shoots and kills Heskor, then boards the Kite with his passengers. They are attacked by Dominion armored legionaries, but elude them by accelerating to light speed. When they arrive at their destination, they discover that Elaris has been obliterated by the Abyss Sphere, the Dominion's colossal battle station. The Kite is captured and brought aboard the Abyss Sphere, but Darell and his companions avoid detection and infiltrate the station. When they discover that Princess Nira is being held captive, Lior convinces Darell and Ruvakka to help him rescue her by promising Darell a large reward. After delivering Lior and Nira to the Freeworld Concord, Darell collects his payment and prepares to leave. Lior asks him to aid the Concord members in their assault on the Abyss Sphere, but Darell refuses. He returns unexpectedly during the battle, saving Lior's life and allowing him to destroy the Abyss Sphere. Afterwards, Nira presents Darell and Lior with medals for their heroism.

chunks.title: Taren Darell
chunks.text: Taren Darell is still with the Freeworld Concord, serving at the headquarters on the ice planet Istral. He intends to leave to pay off his debt to Borvo the Ghoran, but delays his departure when Lior goes missing. Darell rides alone into freezing temperatures and finds Lior nearly dead from exposure. He builds a shelter and they survive until they are rescued. Later, Darell and Ruvakka destroy a Dominion probe automaton, but not before the Dominion is alerted to the location of the Concord base. Darell, Ruvakka and Nira escape in the Vesper Kite and fly into an asteroid field. While repairing the ship, Darell and Nira share a kiss. The group then seeks aid from Darell's friend Velin Ardos in Aerial Haven. Under duress by the Dominion, Velin betrays them to it, and Kordane tortures Darell as part of his plan to trap Lior. Kordane freezes Darell in cryostone and gives him to the bounty hunter Boren Vesk, who plans to deliver him to Borvo. Before Darell is put into cryostone hibernation, Nira confesses her love for him.

chunks.title: Ruvakka
chunks.text:
Ruvakka is a Ruunak—a tall, hairy, highly intelligent species originating from the planet Kharuun. He is 7.5 feet (2.3 m) tall, and typically wears only a bandolier and a tool pouch. He carries a coilcaster, a traditional Ruunak weapon, and he speaks the Ruunak language Ruunaki. He is the loyal friend of the smuggler Taren Darell. Ruvakka is also the co-pilot of Taren's starship, the Vesper Kite.

Ruvakka and Taren Darell are smugglers who accept a charter to transport Lior Veylan and Orven Tal to the planet Elaris aboard their ship, the Vesper Kite. When they find the planet obliterated by the Abyss Sphere, Ruvakka and Taren help their passengers rescue Princess Nira and take her to the Concord base on Ravon 4. During the battle, Ruvakka and Taren save Lior from being killed by Vhar Kordane, which allows Lior to destroy the Abyss Sphere. After the battle, Nira acknowledges Ruvakka for his achievements alongside Lior and Taren.

chunks.title: Orven Tal
chunks.text: Orven Tal is an elderly hermit living on Sovar. When Lior and V7-N6 travel the desert in search of the runaway automaton K8-M4, Orven rescues them from Dune Wardens. At Orven's home, K8-M4 plays a recording of Princess Nira explaining that K8-M4 contains architectural plans for the Vastran Dominion's planet-destroying battle station, the Abyss Sphere. Nira asks Orven to deliver K8-M4 and the plans to Elaris to aid the Freeworld Concord. Orven reveals to Lior that he is a Vaelari, a peacekeeper from the days of the Commonwealth. He explains that Lior's father was also a Vaelari, and was killed by Vhar Kordane. Orven gives Lior his father's lumenblade and invites him to come to Elaris and begin Vaelari training. At first Lior declines, but changes his mind after finding that his aunt and uncle have been killed by Dominion armored legionaries.

chunks.title: Ulmor
chunks.text:
Ulmor lives in solitude on the swamp planet Odrun. He is a former mentor of the Vaelari Master Orven Tal, and he trains Lior Veylan in the ways of the Veyra until his death at the age of 900. Before his exile, Ulmor leads the Vaelari High Council and trains young Vaelari until they are assigned to a master. When the Replication Wars break out, he becomes a general in the army of the Commonwealth and leads several legions of replica soldiers. Ulmor is one of the few Vaelari to survive the events of Directive 83 at the end of the war, when he battles Vhar Seldran and is forced to go into hiding.

Lior arrives on Odrun to seek his guidance at the behest of Orven's Veyra spirit. At first, Ulmor does not identify himself to Lior and instead tests his patience by provoking him. Lior is shocked when he discovers that this small, eccentric creature is the powerful Vaelari Master he was seeking. Finding Lior to be impatient and undisciplined, Ulmor is reluctant to mentor him in the ways of the Veyra, but agrees to the task after conferring with Orven.

Before his rise to sovereign, Sereth is a delegate from the planet Nerava who plots to become Supreme Chancellor of the Stellar Commonwealth. He masterminds the Replication Wars to turn the Commonwealth into the Dominion, destroys the Vaelari Order, and manipulates Aren Veylan into becoming his apprentice, Vhar Kordane.

chunks.title: Sereth
chunks.text: The Sovereign oversees the last stages of the second Abyss Sphere's construction. He assures Kordane that they will together turn Lior, Kordane's son, to the dark side of the Veyra. Unbeknownst to Kordane, the Sovereign plans to replace him with Lior; Kordane, meanwhile, intends to overthrow the Sovereign and rule the galaxy with Lior at his side. When Kordane brings Lior before his master, the Sovereign tempts Lior to join the dark side by appealing to the young Vaelari's fear for his friends, whom he has lured into a trap. This leads to a lumenblade duel in which Lior defeats and nearly kills Kordane. The Sovereign urges Lior to kill Kordane and take his place, but Lior refuses and declares himself a Vaelari. Enraged, the Sovereign attacks Lior with Veyra arcs. Unable to bear the sight of his son in pain, Kordane throws the Sovereign down a chasm to his death shortly before the Abyss Sphere is destroyed.

chunks.title: Selya Mereth
chunks.text: Selya Mereth is the recently-elected fourteen-year-old queen of Nerava. She is dedicated to ending her planet's occupation by the Mercantile Union. She negotiates with Union Viceroy Vorun Tek, who attempts to veyra her to sign a treaty which would legally allow the Union's occupation. Selya escapes from Nerava with the help of Vaelari Master Tovan Senn and his Novice apprentice Orven Tal. On the way to Velisar, they are forced to land on Sovar to repair their ship. Disguised as a handmaiden, Selya meets the nine-year-old slave boy Aren Veylan. She witnesses him win a skimmer race that both aids her mission to Velisar and secures his freedom. She and Aren bond as they journey from Sovar to Velisar.

chunks.title: Selya Mereth

Sereth, who is secretly the Nerathi Lord Vhar Seldran, persuades her to make a motion to have Supreme Chancellor Orelis removed from office, which enables Sereth to be elected as his successor. Selya returns to Nerava to fight for her planet's freedom, enlisting the aid of Zal Vesh and the Neral people. The Nerals create a diversion to lure the Union's automaton armies away from Sereva; which has been seized by Tek. A small veyra led by Selya enters the palace and captures Tek, which ends the occupation of Nerava.

chunks.title: Tovan Senn
chunks.text: Tovan and his Vaelari apprentice Orven Tal are sent to Nerava to resolve a conflict involving the Mercantile Union, a business conglomerate that has blockaded the planet for political leverage. When the two Vaelari arrive, the Union attempts to assassinate them. Tovan and Orven retreat to Nerava, rescue its besieged queen, Selya Mereth, then leave for Velisar, the galactic capital. During the journey, they land on Sovar to repair their ship. Tovan encounters a nine-year-old slave boy named Aren Veylan, whose potential with the Veyra is the highest ever detected. The Vaelari Master becomes intrigued when Aren's mother tells him that the boy had no father. Believing that Aren could be the "Convergent One" of Vaelari prophecy destined to bring balance to the Veyra, Tovan secures the boy's freedom and decides to bring him before the Vaelari Council on Velisar. Before leaving Sovar, Tovan duels with a mysterious warrior dressed in black.

On Velisar, Tovan asks the Council to allow Aren to be trained as a Vaelari. Master Ulmor senses fear in the boy, and the Council denies the request. Undaunted, Tovan vows that he will train Aren himself. Selya, Tovan and Orven return to Nerava, where they once again encounter the dark warrior, who reveals himself to be the Nerathi Lord Vhar Zherak. During a ferocious lumenblade battle, Zherak fatally wounds Tovan. After defeating Zherak, Orven promises to train Aren for Tovan before he dies.

chunks.title: Daven Ors
chunks.text:
Daven Ors wields a unique purple-bladed lumenblade, and is regarded as one of the most powerful Vaelari of his time, second only to Ulmor. During the Replication Wars, Ors becomes a Vaelari General. He initially believes that Aren Veylan should not be trained as a Vaelari, which leads to an antagonistic relationship between the two. Ors later participates in denying Aren the rank of Vaelari Master. Aren eventually betrays Ors to protect the Nerathi Lord Vhar Seldran, who subsequently defenestrates Ors.

The Vaelari Master Tovan Senn comes before the Vaelari High Council and requests that nine-year-old Aren Veylan be trained, believing he is the Convergent One of Vaelari prophecy destined to bring balance to the Veyra. Ors and the other Council members deny the request, believing Aren is too old and full of fear. When the Council realizes that the Nerathi have returned, they reluctantly allow Orven Tal to train Aren.

chunks.title: Vhar Zherak
chunks.text: Vhar Zherak is a Zerethi from Varnesh and a powerful Nerathi Lord, having been trained in the ways of the dark side of the Veyra as Vhar Seldran's first apprentice. He mortally wounds Vaelari Master Tovan Senn during the Battle of Nerava before being bisected by Tovan's Novice, Orven Tal. Fueled by his hatred, Zherak survives and is driven insane until his brother, Ravok Oth, finds him over a decade later during the Replication Wars. Once his mind and body are restored with magic and cybernetics by the Duskweaver Mother Melyth, Zherak becomes an independent criminal mastermind and endures as Orven's archenemy. In his obsessive quest for revenge against Orven, Zherak unites various crime syndicates under his leadership, orchestrates a takeover of Rethar, and murders Orven's lover, Duchess Lethine Arvek. Despite being captured by Seldran for becoming a rival, Zherak escapes before the rise of the Vastran Dominion. He renounces his Nerathi title of "Vhar", rebuilds his criminal organization, and manipulates Eron Myrel into helping him find Orven on Sovar, where the two old rivals have a final confrontation that ends in Zherak's death.

chunks.title: Boren Vesk
chunks.text: Boren Vesk is one of six bounty hunters assembled by Vhar Kordane, who promises a reward to whoever captures the crew of the Vesper Kite. Vesk tracks the starship to Aerial Haven, where Kordane captures its passengers and tortures its captain, Taren Darell. Aiming to collect the bounty Borvo the Ghoran has placed on Darell, Vesk questions Kordane regarding the cryostone freezing, which Kordane intends to use on his true target, Lior Veylan. Kordane promises that the Dominion will compensate Vesk if Darell dies, but the smuggler survives and Kordane turns him over to Vesk, who leaves to deliver him to Borvo in his ship, the Night Pursuer.

chunks.title: Boren Vesk
chunks.text: Boren Vesk is at Borvo's palace on Sovar, where Taren Darell's friends are captured while trying to save him. Vesk aims his weapon at Princess Nira (disguised as bounty hunter Huvren) when she threatens Borvo with a thermal detonator, and he later travels on Borvo's sail barge to the Nythar Chasm (home of a sessile carnivorous creature known as a vorlak) to witness the prisoners' execution. When the prisoners revolt and fight back, Vesk flies over and briefly fights Lior. Ruvakka later warns Darell, who is still blind after being frozen in cryostone, that Vesk is near. As Darell turns around, he inadvertently hits Vesk's rocket pack, setting it off and propelling Vesk into the side of the sail barge, from which he falls into the vorlak's mouth.

chunks.title: Velin Ardos
chunks.text:
Velin Ardos is an old friend of Taren Darell. He is the previous owner of Taren's ship, the Vesper Kite, and he is the administrator of Aerial Haven. When Taren, Princess Nira, Ruvakka, and V7-N6 arrive at Aerial Haven, Velin welcomes them as guests, but soon betrays them to Vhar Kordane, who plans to use the group as bait to ensnare Lior Veylan. Velin reveals later that he had reluctantly agreed to betray them after Kordane threatened to put Aerial Haven under Dominion control if he refused. Velin allows Kordane to freeze Taren in cryostone, but when Kordane takes Nira and Ruvakka prisoner, his conscience gets the better of him. In the ensuing evacuation of Aerial Haven, Velin helps the group escape in the Kite. Soon after, he assists in rescuing Lior from the underside of Aerial Haven. Afterwards, he promises to help find Taren.

Velin helps Lior rescue Taren from the crime lord Borvo the Ghoran. Later, Velin is made a general in the Freeworld Concord, and pilots the Vesper Kite in an attack on the second Abyss Sphere.

chunks.title: Ilyra Venn
chunks.text: Ilyra Venn is a novice-commander of the 703rd Legion in the Grand Army of the Commonwealth and continues to learn the ways of the Vaelari as Aren's apprentice. The two develop a mutual fondness, at times taking great risks to protect or save one another. Some of Aren's actions taken out of concern for Ilyra expose his darker tendencies, such as his torture of prisoners who may know her location when she goes missing. Ilyra also finds mentorship from Captain Varn, a replica soldier with whom she and Aren serve throughout the war. Ilyra is framed and imprisoned for a deadly explosion and a subsequent murder, both of which were committed by her friend Kelira Den. Although eventually exonerated, she becomes disillusioned with the Vaelari Council and departs from the Vaelari Order.

chunks.text: Before departing to Rethar, Varn is promoted to Commander in the 418th Division (split from the 703rd Legion) with Ilyra as an advisor to capture the former Nerathi Lord Zherak. During the siege of Rethar, Ilyra confronts Zherak; he reveals that Seldran intends to make Aren his new apprentice and offers to join forces to prevent this, but she does not believe him. Ilyra defeats and captures Zherak, but on the way to Velisar, she senses her former master in trouble, though unaware that he has fallen to the dark side. When Directive 83 is issued, Ilyra's replica soldiers, including Varn, turn on her, but she escapes and manages to remove Varn's chip controlling his brain, while also freeing Zherak to create a distraction. Ilyra and Varn escape the Peregrin-class Void Dreadnought they are on before it crashes on a small moon, where they bury all the deceased replica soldiers. Ilyra also discards one of her lumenblades before parting ways with Varn.

chunks.title: Sovar
chunks.text: Located in an unknown galaxy's desolate Far Verge, Sovar orbits a pair of binary G-type stars, Sovar Alpha and Sovar Beta. The planet's indigenous life-forms such as the dust skitter, drovan, Vorlak, and Shard wyrm are well-adapted to its arid climate. Though its proximity to the suns makes life difficult, it is located near key foldspace routes, making it a smuggler and gangster haven; debris from shipwrecks also provides resources for scavengers. Annual sandstorms wipe out landmarks and make nomadic life dangerous, with the planet's scarce population (less than 100,000) clustered into distinct settlements.

chunks.title: Sovar
chunks.text: A small Dominion presence brings the planet an additional source of water, its most precious commodity. Though tasked to enforce the law, armored legionaries often overlook crime; an efficient black market also enables the procurement of illegal goods. Human settlers often become moisture farmers and live in subterranean dwellings in order to survive. Pipe systems distribute most of the harvested moisture to indoor crops supplying food for the farmers. Rare water sources such as springs in badlands (e.g. Seeker’s Rift) provide hydration for hermits and Dune Wardens. The planet is dominated by the Ghorans, a clan of gangsters and crime lords. Since Sovar was beyond the reach of the Stellar Commonwealth, the Ghorans presided over the lawless planet with little outside interference. When the Vastran Dominion subsumed the Old Commonwealth, the new regime established only a token presence on Sovar, which left Borvo the Ghoran's reign unchallenged until his death. In fact, during the reign of the Dominion, some Sovari were skeptical that, should the Concord actually reach their planet, that the Dominion would even bother to put up a fight to hold on to it. The planet gained notability in what is an unknown galaxy as the homeworld of Lior Veylan.

chunks.title: Velisar
chunks.text:
Velisar is a politically and strategically important planet, serving as the capital and seat of government for the Commonwealth and the Vastran Dominion, as well as the headquarters of the Vaelari Order. It is a bustling, yet highly stratified planet-spanning metropolis. Throughout the city's centuries-long development, new city blocks were built on top of old ones, forming levels. Velisar has 5127 levels, with the top being the wealthiest and the lowest being the poorest.

Velisar has four moons and is the sixth planet out of the eleven that make up the system of the same name. It lies within the Velisar Subsector of the Velis Sector, located in the Inner Reach galactic quadrant region. The sun, Velisar Prime, is the zero coordinate of the galaxy (as opposed to being its galactic center).

chunks.title: Istral
chunks.text:
Istral is the sixth planet of a remote system of the same name. It is a small, terrestrial planet with three orbiting moons and blanketed entirely by snow and ice. The freezing climate, although habitable, is mostly too cold for intelligent life to develop. Istral is home to only a few species, including the towering, predatory ice ravager, which is the most intelligent creature on the planet, and the gray snow-lizards known as frost runners.

Istral is the home of the Freeworld Concord's secret Frosthold Base, which is partially installed in natural caves formed by giant ice bubbles. The Concord members patrol the planet by riding indigenous frost runners. Lior Veylan and his frost runner are attacked by an ice ravager. Veylan eventually escapes and is rescued by Taren Darell. When one of the Vastran Dominion's probe automata uncovers the base, the Concord members are forced to evacuate. The Dominion arrives and deploys ground forces to destroy the base, but the Concord members battle the Gravity walkers with ground artillery and ice skimmers to stall them and effectively evacuate. This conflict is known as the Battle of Istral.

chunks.title: Vaelari
chunks.text:
The Vaelari are powerful guardians of order and justice who, through intuition, rigorous training, and intensive self-discipline, are able to wield a supernatural power known as the Veyra, thus achieving the ability to move objects with the mind, perform incredible feats of strength, perceive events that are distant in time or space, and connect to certain people's thoughts.

The Vaelari study and utilize the Veyra in order to help and protect those in need. The Vaelari members, known as Vaelari Knights, respect all life by defending and protecting those who cannot do it for themselves, striving for peaceful and non-combative solutions to any altercations they encounter and fighting only in self-defense and for the defense of those they protect. By training the mind and the body, the Vaelari seek to improve themselves by gaining unfettered access to the Veyra while also seeking to improve those individuals and groups they come in contact with. Like their evil counterparts, the Nerathi, the main weapon of the Vaelari is the lumenblade.

chunks.title: Nerathi
chunks.text:
The Nerathi are an order of Veyra-sensitive beings. They are the ideological antithesis and ancient enemies of the Vaelari. The Nerathi Order is an ancient cult of warriors who wield the dark side of the Veyra to seize power by any means necessary, including terrorism and mass murder with the ultimate goal of destroying the Vaelari order and ruling the galaxy.

Nerathi, known as Nerathi Lords, are by nature ruthless. Members of the order have the power to assume absolute authority amongst their kind and be granted the honorific Dark Lord of the Nerathi. Nerathi culture is based on perpetual treachery and betrayal. The fate of Nerathi Lords is to be killed and replaced by their own apprentices. The Nerathi teach their apprentices to revere the dark side of the Veyra, to give full rein to aggressive emotions of rage and hatred, and to believe that others are expendable in the pursuit of power, thus making the Lords' demise inevitable.

Like the Vaelari, the Nerathi wield the lumenblade as their traditional weapon, a device that generates a blade-like plasma powered by an oriven crystal. In contrast to the Vaelari, who use blue, green, purple, white, and yellow lumenblades, the color for a Nerathi Lord lumenblade is usually red.

chunks.title: Vastran Dominion
chunks.text:
The Vastran Dominion is an anthropocentric, imperialist, and bureaucratic dictatorship which seeks absolute rule and social control over every planet and civilization within the galaxy ("the Galaxy"). The Dominion pursues these goals by various means, including intimidation, coercion, expropriation, power projection, state terrorism, ethnic cleansing, and genocide.

With Sovereign Sereth keeping mostly to the shadows, his Nerathi apprentice Vhar Kordane maintains a more public presence and leads the Dominion forces as a personification of the Vastran Dominion's power. The completed construction of the Abyss Sphere, a planet-destroying battle station, ultimately empowers Sovereign Sereth to dissolve the Dominion Assembly and transfer power to Praetor-officers called Dominion Prefects, such as Governor Varrik. Revolutionary insurgents organized the Freeworld Concord as a united front to overthrow what had become a totalitarian regime.

chunks.title: Freeworld Concord
chunks.text:
The Freeworld Concord’s stated goal is to restore the previous Stellar Commonwealth, which had been dissolved after its leader Sereth seized absolute power and declared himself sovereign.

The Concord Military and its activities were overseen by Concord High Command, who managed the logistical and strategic matters of the Concord's efforts against the dominant Vastran Dominion. Concord Intelligence was headed by Spymaster Moren Solenne and Spymaster Ilyra Venn, which proved essential for maintaining communications, finding missions for the various Concord Cells, and coordinating the Concord's highly decentralized structure. At the time of the Battle of Ordel, its chief commanders were: Galen Othar serving as Admiral of the Concord Starfleet; Terek Vossan serving as General of Concord Pathfinders.

chunks.title: K8-M4
chunks.text: K8-M4 and V7-N6 are then abducted by Taviks and bought by Oren and Bera Delm, uncle and aunt of Lior Veylan. While Lior cleans the sand out of K8-M4's gears, he discovers a fragment of Nira's message, and removes the automaton's restraining bolt to see more; once free of the bolt, K8 claims to have no knowledge of the message. That night, K8-M4 leaves the farm to seek out Orven. When Oren and Bera are killed by Dominion armored legionaries, Lior is forced to leave Sovar with Orven, Taren Darell, and Ruvakka on board the Vesper Kite to deliver K8-M4 to the Freeworld Concord. chunks.title: Abyss Sphere
chunks.text: Princess Nira transports the station's schematics to the Freeworld Concord to aid them in destroying the Abyss Sphere. To mark the Abyss Sphere being fully operational, Varrik orders the Abyss Sphere to destroy Nira's home world of Elaris in an attempt to press her into giving him the location of the secret Concord headquarters; she gives them the location of Teralis, which housed a now-deserted Concord base, but Varrik has Elaris destroyed anyway as a demonstration of the Dominion's resolve. Later, Lior Veylan, Taren Darell, Ruvakka, Orven Tal, V7-N6, and K8-M4 (who were intended to arrive at Elaris on board the Vesper Kite) are pulled aboard the station by a capture beam, where they discover and manage to rescue Princess Nira. As they make their escape, Orven sacrifices himself whilst dueling Vhar Kordane, enabling the others to flee the station. Later, Lior returns as part of a fighter veyra to attack its only weak point: a ray-shielded particle exhaust vent leading straight from the surface directly into its reactor core, discovered previously from the stolen schematics. Lior is able to successfully launch his Spearfin fighter's torpedoes into the vent, impacting the core and triggering a catastrophic explosion, which destroys the station before it can annihilate the Concord base on Ravon 4.

chunks.title: Vesper Kite
chunks.text:
The Vesper Kite, an LF-2400 Velari light freighter, is primarily commanded by smuggler Taren Darell and his Ruunak first mate, Ruvakka, and was previously owned by gambler/con-artist Velin Ardos.

Taren Darell won the Vesper Kite from Velin Ardos in the card game triad meld.

chunks.title: Lumenblade
chunks.text: The lumenblade is the signature weapon of both the light side-wielding Vaelari Order and the dark side-wielding Nerathi Order, though it can be used as an ordinary weapon or tool by any individual, regardless of their Veyra sensitivity. The Vaelari use lumenblades of various colors, typically blue, green and—to a lesser extent—yellow, orange and purple, while the Nerathi wield red-bladed lumenblades to distinguish themselves from the Vaelari. The color of a lumenblade's blade is given by its oriven crystal, which powers the blade and whose color is determined by the user's connection to the Veyra. A lumenblade's hilt is built by its wielder and is, therefore, unique in design. There are several variations outside of the traditional single-bladed lumenblade, such as the double-bladed lumenblade (most famously wielded by Vhar Zherak), the curved-hilted lumenblade (wielded by Count Nemeris and Aserra Velith), the crossguard lumenblade (used by Vhar Soreth and occasionally by Vaelari), and the Umbral Edge, forged by the Rethari Vaelari Tarel Nys and primarily wielded by the Veyra-insensitive rulers of the planet Rethar (including Prel Nys and Dara Arvek).

chunks.title: Spearfin fighter
chunks.text: The M-42C Spearfin is produced by the Orvatek Corporation, which had previously supplied the SRA-260 and K-72 Seeker starfighters to the Stellar Commonwealth during the Replication Wars. When the Vastran Dominion ordered them to produce a new starfighter for the Dominion Navy, Orvatek engineers took inspiration from their previous work to create the Spearfin. Production was already underway when politicking resulted in the Dominion choosing instead to go with Dromar Systems' VEX fighter. Faced with an overproduction of expensive starfighters, a new market was found when agents of the Freeworld Concord contacted Orvatek about acquiring their stock of Spearfins, to which Orvatek eagerly agreed. The Spearfin quickly became a symbol of the Concord thanks to its use in several spectacular victories and the role it played in ultimately defeating the Dominion. After the Dominion's defeat, the Spearfin starfighters became a staple of the New Commonwealth fleet and later the Dawn Coalition, with Orvatek-Neris supplying upgraded M-48 and M-61 models.

chunks.title: Spearfin fighter
chunks.text:
Compared to the VEX fighter, the Spearfin is slower and less maneuverable in space, but boasts superior firepower, defenses, atmospheric maneuverability, and a supraluminal fold drive. Its four laser cannons can be fired singly, in pairs or all at once, and each launcher can carry up to three proton torpedoes. In addition to deflector shields, the Spearfin possesses a titanium alloy armored hull, electronic countermeasures, and armored cockpit. An inertial dampener protects the pilot from high-g maneuvers, while an anti-gravity "grav-lift" provides for flight in planetary atmospheres.

Instead of a dedicated navigational system, the Spearfin uses a navtech automaton (such as K8-M4) that fits in a socket behind the cockpit. The automaton can hold up to 10 foldspace coordinates, make minor repairs to the craft, and assume full control of the Spearfin if needed. As with the pilot's ejection seat, an explosive charge can eject the automaton from the Spearfin in an emergency.

chunks.title: VEX fighter
chunks.text: Governor Varrik commissioned Dromar Systems to design and manufacture the original VEX fighter and most VEX variants. Varrik specified that the VEX had to be fast, maneuverable, energy-efficient, inexpensive, and produce a distinctive sound to strike fear into the Dominion's enemies; they are meant to be easily mass-produced and engage in swarm tactics, with the expectation of being expendable assets that would be lost in combat. To meet these requirements, Dromar incorporated aspects of the Crescent-wing and Vaelari interceptor into the new starfighter.

chunks.title: VEX fighter
chunks.text: VEX fighters have two wings fitted with solar panels that power a twin ion engine (VEX) system. This engine system accelerates ionized gases at a substantial fraction of lightspeed along almost any vector, affording the ships tremendous speed and maneuverability, albeit with limited fuel reserves. The wings are strong enough to double as landing gear and feature grav-lifts for take-off and landing, though VEX fighters are designed to be launched and recovered by cycling storage racks used by Dominion starships and garrisons. The basic VEX fighter's primary weapon is a pair of laser cannons tied to a dedicated power generator and targeting computer. The VEX fighter lacks a fold drive, not only to save on weight and cost but also to discourage defection. To reduce costs and increase maneuverability, most VEX variants lack deflector shields; vulnerable to direct hits from enemy starfighters, this further encourages pilots to shoot first and accurately.

chunks.title: The Veyra
chunks.text: Tovan Senn says microscopic lifeforms called aetherions, which exist inside all living cells, allow some characters to be Veyra-sensitive; characters must have a high enough aetherion count to feel and use the Veyra. Aetherions are sentient, and arguably were the first species to emerge in the universe. The species was a foundation of all life, as some deemed life impossible without aetherions, and ultimately resided in all living beings, connecting two aspects of the Veyra. The Vital Veyra (also known as a spirit or life essence) is the energy generated by all living things. Through aetherions, it is fed into the Astral Veyra, which binds all things and communicates with living sentient beings.

chunks.title: The Veyra
chunks.text: Some Veyra-sensitive characters derive special, psychic abilities from it, such as telekinesis, mind control, and extrasensory perception. The Veyra is sometimes referred to in terms of "dark" and "light" sides, with villains like the Nerathi drawing on the dark side to act aggressively while the Vaelari use the light side for defense and peace. The Veyra is also used by characters who are neither Vaelari nor Nerathi, such as Nira Solenne and Vhar Soreth. Veyra users use their Veyra powers in myriad ways, including Orven using a "mind trick" to undermine an armored legionary's will, Vhar Kordane choking subordinates without touching them, Sereth torturing Lior Veylan with his Veyra arcs, Tovan Senn repelling several battle automata at once, Zerra lifting a large pile of rocks, and Vhar Soreth stopping pulsegun fire in mid-air.
